documents.title: NIST Special Publication 800-52 Revision 2: Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of Transport Layer Security (TLS) Implementations
NIST Special Publication 800-131A Revision 2: Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths

extractions.exact_source_text: Deviations from these guidelines are acceptable, provided that agencies and system administrators assess and accept the risks associated with alternative configurations in terms of both security and interoperability.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: provided that agencies and system administrators assess and accept the risks associated with alternative configurations in terms of both security and interoperability
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: None

extractions.exact_source_text: In order to comply with these guidelines, both the client and the server must be configured for data confidentiality and integrity services.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: eavesdropping; unauthorized data modification (deletion, addition, or modification of data); forgery; replay attacks
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: both the client and the server must be configured for data confidentiality and integrity services

extractions.exact_source_text: The sequence number of the current message must be greater than the sequence number of the previous message in order to further process the message.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: except when 0-RTT data (optionally sent in the first flight of handshake messages) is sent in TLS 1.3
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The sequence number of the current message must be greater than the sequence number of the previous message in order to further process the message

extractions.exact_source_text: Since the random numbers generated by the client and server contribute to the randomness of the session keys, the client and server must be capable of generating random numbers with at least 112 bits of security each.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the client and server must be capable of generating random numbers with at least 112 bits of security each

extractions.exact_source_text: Implementation requirements indicate that federal agencies shall not procure TLS server implementations unless they include the required functionality or can be augmented with additional commercial products to meet the requirements.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: unless they include the required functionality or can be augmented with additional commercial products to meet the requirements
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: federal agencies shall not procure TLS server implementations unless they include the required functionality or can be augmented with additional commercial products to meet the requirements

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that support government-only applications shall be configured to use TLS 1.2 and should be configured to use TLS 1.3 as well.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that support government-only applications shall be configured to use TLS 1.2 and should be configured to use TLS 1.3 as well

extractions.exact_source_text: These servers should not be configured to use TLS 1.1 and shall not use TLS 1.0, SSL 3.0, or SSL 2.0.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: These servers should not be configured to use TLS 1.1 and shall not use TLS 1.0, SSL 3.0, or SSL 2.0

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that support citizen or business-facing applications (i.e., the client may not be part of a government IT system) shall be configured to negotiate TLS 1.2 and should be configured to negotiate TLS 1.3. The use of TLS versions 1.1 and 1.0 is generally discouraged, but these versions may be configured when necessary to enable interaction with citizens and businesses.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: these versions may be configured when necessary to enable interaction with citizens and businesses
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: shall be configured to negotiate TLS 1.2 and should be configured to negotiate TLS 1.3

extractions.exact_source_text: These servers shall not allow the use of SSL 2.0 or SSL 3.0.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: These servers shall not allow the use of SSL 2.0 or SSL 3.0

extractions.exact_source_text: Agencies shall support TLS 1.3 by January 1, 2024. After this date, servers shall support TLS 1.3 for both government-only and citizen or business-facing applications.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Transition date: January 1, 2024
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Agencies shall support TLS 1.3 by January 1, 2024. After this date, servers shall support TLS 1.3 for both government-only and citizen or business-facing applications

extractions.exact_source_text: In general, servers that support TLS 1.3 should be configured to use TLS 1.2 as well. However, TLS 1.2 may be disabled on servers that support TLS 1.3 if it has been determined that TLS 1.2 is not needed for interoperability.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: TLS 1.2 may be disabled on servers that support TLS 1.3 if it has been determined that TLS 1.2 is not needed for interoperability
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: servers that support TLS 1.3 should be configured to use TLS 1.2 as well

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that incorrectly implement TLS version negotiation shall not be used.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: version negotiation failure; terminate the connection when the client offers a version newer than TLS 1.0
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that incorrectly implement TLS version negotiation shall not be used

extractions.exact_source_text: The TLS server shall be configured with one or more public-key certificates and the associated private keys. TLS server implementations should support the use of multiple server certificates with their associated private keys to support algorithm and key size agility.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The TLS server shall be configured with one or more public-key certificates and the associated private keys. TLS server implementations should support the use of multiple server certificates with their associated private keys

extractions.exact_source_text: At a minimum, TLS servers conforming to this specification shall be configured with an RSA signature certificate or an ECDSA signature certificate.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: The other certificate types and their associated cipher suites are not commonly used, especially in externally-accessible servers, but are included in these guidelines for completeness and to cover edge cases
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: shall be configured with an RSA signature certificate or an ECDSA signature certificate

extractions.exact_source_text: If the server is configured with an ECDSA signature certificate, either curve P-256 or curve P-384 should be used for the public key in the certificate.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: either curve P-256 or curve P-384 should be used for the public key in the certificate

extractions.exact_source_text: TLS servers shall be configured with certificates issued by a CA that publishes revocation information in Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) [63] responses. The CA may additionally publish revocation information in a certificate revocation list (CRL) [19]. The source(s) for the revocation information shall be included in the CA-issued certificate in the appropriate extension to promote interoperability.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: The CA may additionally publish revocation information in a certificate revocation list (CRL)
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: TLS servers shall be configured with certificates issued by a CA that publishes revocation information in Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) [63] responses... The source(s) for the revocation information shall be included in the CA-issued certificate in the appropriate extension

extractions.exact_source_text: To comply with these guidelines, the TLS server certificate shall be an X.509 version 3 certificate; both the public key contained in the certificate and the signature shall provide at least 112 bits of security.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the TLS server certificate shall be an X.509 version 3 certificate; both the public key contained in the certificate and the signature shall provide at least 112 bits of security

extractions.exact_source_text: If the server supports TLS versions prior to TLS 1.2, the certificate should be signed with an algorithm consistent with the public key: Certificates containing RSA, ECDSA, or DSA public keys should be signed with those same signature algorithms, respectively; Certificates containing Diffie-Hellman public keys should be signed with DSA; and Certificates containing ECDH public keys should be signed with ECDSA.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: If the server supports TLS versions prior to TLS 1.2
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the certificate should be signed with an algorithm consistent with the public key

extractions.exact_source_text: There is a key purpose specifically for server authentication, and the server should be configured to allow its use.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the server should be configured to allow its use

extractions.exact_source_text: In the absence of agency-specific certificate profile requirements, this certificate profile should be used for the server certificate.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: In the absence of agency-specific certificate profile requirements
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: this certificate profile should be used for the server certificate

extractions.exact_source_text: Issuer Distinguished Name (DN): A single value should be encoded in each Relative Distinguished Name (RDN). All attributes that are of DirectoryString type should be encoded as a PrintableString.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: A single value should be encoded in each Relative Distinguished Name (RDN). All attributes that are of DirectoryString type should be encoded as a PrintableString

extractions.exact_source_text: Validity Period: 3 years or less; Dates through 2049 expressed in UTCTime
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: 3 years or less; Dates through 2049 expressed in UTCTime

extractions.exact_source_text: Subject Distinguished Name: A single value should be encoded in each RDN. All attributes that are of DirectoryString type should be encoded as a PrintableString. If present, the CN attribute should be of the form: CN={host IP address | host DNS name}
extractions.explicit_exceptions: If present, the CN attribute should be of the form: CN={host IP address | host DNS name}
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: A single value should be encoded in each RDN. All attributes that are of DirectoryString type should be encoded as a PrintableString. If present, the CN attribute should be of the form: CN={host IP address | host DNS name}

extractions.exact_source_text: Authority Key Identifier: Prohibited: Issuer DN, Serial Number tuple
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Prohibited: Issuer DN, Serial Number tuple

extractions.exact_source_text: Key Usage: Critical: Yes; digitalSignature (RSA signature certificate, ECDSA signature certificate, or DSA signature certificate); keyAgreement (ECDH certificate, DH certificate)
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Values by certificate type
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Critical: Yes

extractions.exact_source_text: Extended Key Usage: Critical: No; id-kp-serverAuth {1 3 6 1 5 5 7 3 1}: Required; id-kp-clientAuth {1 3 6 1 5 5 7 3 2}: Optional; Prohibited: anyExtendedKeyUsage; all others unless consistent with key usage extension
extractions.explicit_exceptions: all others unless consistent with key usage extension
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: id-kp-serverAuth Required; Prohibited: anyExtendedKeyUsage

extractions.exact_source_text: Subject Alternative Name (SAN): Critical: No; DNS host name, or IP address if there is no DNS name assigned. Other name forms may be included, if appropriate. Required. Multiple SANs are permitted, e.g., for load balanced environments.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: IP address if there is no DNS name assigned. Other name forms may be included, if appropriate
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: DNS host name, or IP address if there is no DNS name assigned... Required

extractions.exact_source_text: Authority Information Access: Critical: No; id-ad-caIssuers: Required. Access method entry contains HTTP URL for certificates issued to issuing CA; id-ad-ocsp: Required. Access method entry contains HTTP URL for the issuing CA OCSP responder
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: id-ad-caIssuers Required... id-ad-ocsp Required

extractions.exact_source_text: CRL Distribution Points: Critical: No; Optional. HTTP value in distributionPoint field pointing to a full and complete CRL. Prohibited: reasons and cRLIssuer fields, and nameRelativetoCRLIssuer CHOICE
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Optional
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Prohibited: reasons and cRLIssuer fields, and nameRelativetoCRLIssuer CHOICE

extractions.exact_source_text: The server shall perform revocation checking of the client certificate when client authentication is used. Revocation information shall be obtained by the server from one or more of the following locations: 1. Certificate Revocation List (CRL) or OCSP [63] response in the server’s local store; 2. OCSP response from a locally-configured OCSP responder; 3. OCSP response from the OCSP responder location identified in the OCSP field in the Authority Information Access extension in the client certificate; or 4. CRL from the CRL Distribution Points extension in the client certificate.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: when client authentication is used
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall perform revocation checking of the client certificate when client authentication is used. Revocation information shall be obtained by the server from one or more of the following locations: 1. Certificate Revocation List (CRL) or OCSP [63] response in the server’s local store; 2. OCSP response from a locally-configured OCSP responder; 3. OCSP response from the OCSP responder location identified in the OCSP field in the Authority Information Access extension in the client certificate; or 4. CRL from the CRL Distribution Points extension in the client certificate

extractions.exact_source_text: The decision to accept or reject a certificate in this situation should be made according to agency policy.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: When the local store does not have the current or a cogent CRL or OCSP response and the OCSP responder and the CRL distribution point are unavailable or inaccessible at the time of TLS session establishment
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: accept a potentially revoked or compromised certificate
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The decision to accept or reject a certificate in this situation should be made according to agency policy

extractions.exact_source_text: When an agency is obtaining a certificate for a TLS server for which all the clients are under the agency’s control, the agency may issue the certificate from its own CA if it can configure the clients to trust that CA. In other cases, the agency should obtain a certificate from a publicly-trusted CA (a CA that clients that will be connecting to the server have already been configured to trust).
extractions.explicit_exceptions: for which all the clients are under the agency’s control
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: threat that the issuing CA can be compromised or that the registration system, persons, or process can be compromised to obtain an unauthorized certificate in the name of a legitimate entity and thus compromise the clients
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the agency should obtain a certificate from a publicly-trusted CA

extractions.exact_source_text: The server shall be configured to only use cipher suites that are composed entirely of NIST-approved algorithms (i.e., [6, 7, 9, 26-28, 44-46, 49]).
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall be configured to only use cipher suites that are composed entirely of NIST-approved algorithms

extractions.exact_source_text: Cipher suites that do not appear in this section, Appendix C, or Appendix D shall not be used.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Appendix C (pre-shared keys) or Appendix D (RSA key transport transition)
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Cipher suites that do not appear in this section, Appendix C, or Appendix D shall not be used

extractions.exact_source_text: When ephemeral keys are used to establish the master secret, each ephemeral key-pair (i.e., the server ephemeral key-pair and the client ephemeral key-pair) shall have at least 112 bits of security.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: each ephemeral key-pair (i.e., the server ephemeral key-pair and the client ephemeral key-pair) shall have at least 112 bits of security

extractions.exact_source_text: Cipher suites that use the Triple Data Encryption Aglorithm (TDEA, also written as 3DES) are no longer allowed due to the limited amounts of data that can be processed under a single key.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: limited amounts of data that can be processed under a single key
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Cipher suites that use the Triple Data Encryption Aglorithm (TDEA, also written as 3DES) are no longer allowed

extractions.exact_source_text: The server shall be configured to only use cipher suites for which it has a valid certificate containing a signature providing at least 112 bits of security.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall be configured to only use cipher suites for which it has a valid certificate containing a signature providing at least 112 bits of security

extractions.exact_source_text: If a subset of the cipher suites that are acceptable for the server certificate(s) are supported, the following list gives general guidance on choosing the strongest options: 1. Prefer ephemeral keys over static keys (i.e., prefer DHE over DH, and prefer ECDHE over ECDH). Ephemeral keys provide perfect forward secrecy. 2. Prefer GCM or CCM modes over CBC mode. The use of an authenticated encryption mode prevents several attacks (see Section 3.3.2 for more information). Note that these are not available in versions prior to TLS 1.2. 3. Prefer CCM over CCM_8. The latter contains a shorter authentication tag, which provides a lower authentication strength.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: This list does not have to be strictly followed, as some environments or applications may have special circumstances
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: compromise of a long-term private key after it has been used to establish a session key; attacks on CBC mode
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Prefer ephemeral keys over static keys... Prefer GCM or CCM modes over CBC mode... Prefer CCM over CCM_8

extractions.exact_source_text: TLS implementations shall use the bad_record_mac error to indicate a padding error when communications are secured using a CBC cipher suite. Implementations shall compute the MAC regardless of whether padding errors exist.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: when communications are secured using a CBC cipher suite
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: timing attacks on CBC cipher suites; attacks on CBC mode that rely on the time to compute the message authentication code (MAC)
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: TLS implementations shall use the bad_record_mac error to indicate a padding error when communications are secured using a CBC cipher suite. Implementations shall compute the MAC regardless of whether padding errors exist

extractions.exact_source_text: TLS implementations should support constant-time decryption or near constant-time decryption.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: TLS implementations should support constant-time decryption or near constant-time decryption

extractions.exact_source_text: The POODLE attack exploits nondeterministic padding in SSL 3.0 [43]. The vulnerability does not exist in the TLS protocols, but the vulnerability can exist in a TLS implementation when the SSL decoder code is reused to process TLS data [38]. TLS implementations shall correctly decode the CBC padding bytes.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: POODLE attack [43]; nondeterministic padding in SSL 3.0
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: TLS implementations shall correctly decode the CBC padding bytes

extractions.exact_source_text: The cryptographic module used by the server shall be a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module [50, 51]. All cryptographic algorithms that are included in the configured cipher suites and the random number generator shall be within the scope of the validation.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The cryptographic module used by the server shall be a FIPS 140-validated cryptographic module... All cryptographic algorithms that are included in the configured cipher suites and the random number generator shall be within the scope of the validation

extractions.exact_source_text: Other than the SHA-1 exception listed for specific instances above, all cryptography used shall provide at least 112 bits of security. All server and client certificates shall contain public keys that offer at least 112 bits of security. All server and client certificates and certificates in their certification paths shall be signed using key pairs that offer at least 112 bits of security and SHA-224 or a stronger hashing algorithm. All ephemeral keys used by the client and server shall offer at least 112 bits of security. All symmetric algorithms used to protect the TLS data shall use keys that offer at least 112 bits of security.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Other than the SHA-1 exception listed for specific instances above (signing ephemeral keys in TLS versions prior to 1.2 and client authentication using digital signatures)
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: all cryptography used shall provide at least 112 bits of security... All server and client certificates shall contain public keys that offer at least 112 bits of security. All server and client certificates and certificates in their certification paths shall be signed using key pairs that offer at least 112 bits of security and SHA-224 or a stronger hashing algorithm. All ephemeral keys used by the client and server shall offer at least 112 bits of security. All symmetric algorithms used to protect the TLS data shall use keys that offer at least 112 bits of security

extractions.exact_source_text: The FIPS 140 validation certificate for the cryptographic module used by the server shall indicate that the random bit generator (RBG) has been validated in accordance with the SP 800-90 series [8, 48, 66].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The FIPS 140 validation certificate for the cryptographic module used by the server shall indicate that the random bit generator (RBG) has been validated in accordance with the SP 800-90 series

extractions.exact_source_text: The validated random number generator shall be used to generate the random bytes of the server random value. The validated random number generator should be used to generate the 4-byte timestamp of the server random value.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: downgrade protection mechanism embedded in the random value that overwrites the last eight bytes
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The validated random number generator shall be used to generate the random bytes of the server random value. The validated random number generator should be used to generate the 4-byte timestamp of the server random value

extractions.exact_source_text: In general, servers should only be configured to support extensions that are required by the application or that enhance security. Extensions that are not needed should not be enabled.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: Heartbleed bug [70]; flaw in an implementation of the heartbeat extension [64]
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: servers should only be configured to support extensions that are required by the application or that enhance security. Extensions that are not needed should not be enabled

extractions.exact_source_text: The server shall support the use of the following TLS extensions: 1. Renegotiation Indication; 2. Server Name Indication; 3. Extended Master Secret; 4. Signature Algorithms; 5. Certificate Status Request extension
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall support the use of the following TLS extensions: 1. Renegotiation Indication; 2. Server Name Indication; 3. Extended Master Secret; 4. Signature Algorithms; 5. Certificate Status Request extension

extractions.exact_source_text: Server implementations shall perform initial and subsequent renegotiations in accordance with RFC 5746 [59] and RFC 8446 [57].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: session renegotiation is vulnerable to an attack in which the attacker forms a TLS connection with the target server, injects content of its choice, and then splices in a new TLS connection from a legitimate client... session splicing or session interception
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Server implementations shall perform initial and subsequent renegotiations in accordance with RFC 5746 [59] and RFC 8446 [57]

extractions.exact_source_text: The server shall be able to process and respond to the server name indication extension received in a ClientHello message as described in [29].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall be able to process and respond to the server name indication extension received in a ClientHello message as described in [29]

extractions.exact_source_text: Bhargavan et al. have shown that an active attacker can synchronize two TLS sessions such that they share the same master secret, thus allowing the attacker to perform a man-in-the-middle attack [12]. The Extended Master Secret extension, specified in RFC 7627 [13], prevents such attacks by binding the master secret to a hashed log of the full handshake. The server shall support the use of this extension.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: man-in-the-middle attack; synchronize two TLS sessions such that they share the same master secret [12]
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The server shall support the use of this extension

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers shall support the processing of the signature algorithms extension received in a ClientHello message.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.2, 1.3
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers shall support the processing of the signature algorithms extension received in a ClientHello message

extractions.exact_source_text: Upon receipt of the status_request extension, a server with a certificate issued by a CA that supports OCSP shall include the certificate status along with its certificate by sending a CertificateStatus message immediately following the Certificate message.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: a server with a certificate issued by a CA that supports OCSP; In TLS 1.3, the server includes the certificate status in the Certificate message
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: shall include the certificate status along with its certificate by sending a CertificateStatus message immediately following the Certificate message

extractions.exact_source_text: When TLS versions prior to TLS 1.2 are supported by the server and TLS version 1.3 is not supported, the fallback SCSV shall be supported.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: When TLS versions prior to TLS 1.2 are supported by the server and TLS version 1.3 is not supported
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: unintended protocol downgrades in versions prior to TLS 1.3; attacker can use an external version negotiation as a means to force unnecessary protocol downgrades
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: the fallback SCSV shall be supported... if the server deems it inappropriate (i.e., the server supports a higher TLS version), the server returns a fatal alert

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that support either ephemeral ECDH cipher suites or TLS 1.3 shall support this extension. When elliptic curve cipher suites are configured, at least one of the NIST-approved curves, P-256 (secp256r1) and P-384 (secp384r1), shall be supported as described in RFC 8422 [52]. Additional NIST-recommended elliptic curves are listed in SP 800-56A, Appendix D [6]. Finite field groups that are approved for TLS in SP 800-56A, Appendix D may be supported.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: None
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that support either ephemeral ECDH cipher suites or TLS 1.3 shall support this extension. When elliptic curve cipher suites are configured, at least one of the NIST-approved curves, P-256 (secp256r1) and P-384 (secp384r1), shall be supported

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that support TLS 1.3 shall support this extension as described in Section 4.2.7 of RFC 8446 [57].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS version 1.3
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that support TLS 1.3 shall support this extension

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that support EC cipher suites with TLS 1.2 and below shall be able to process the supported point format received in the ClientHello message by the client. The servers shall process this extension in accordance with Section 5.1 of RFC 8422 [52]. Servers that support EC cipher suites shall also be able to send the supported EC point format in the ServerHello message as described in Section 5.2 of RFC 8422 [52].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that support EC cipher suites with TLS 1.2 and below shall be able to process the supported point format received in the ClientHello message... shall also be able to send the supported EC point format in the ServerHello message

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that have this capability and have certificates issued by CAs that support OCSP should be configured to support this extension.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2; Servers that have this capability and have certificates issued by CAs that support OCSP
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: should be configured to support this extension

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that communicate with memory-constrained clients and that have been issued certificates by multiple CAs shall be able to process and respond to the trusted CA indication extension received in a ClientHello message as described in [29].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2; Servers that communicate with memory-constrained clients and that have been issued certificates by multiple CAs
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: shall be able to process and respond to the trusted CA indication extension received in a ClientHello message

extractions.exact_source_text: Servers that are configured to negotiate CBC cipher suites shall support this extension as described in [33].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS versions: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2; Servers that are configured to negotiate CBC cipher suites
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: Several attacks on CBC cipher suites have been possible due to the MAC-then-encrypt order of operations
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Servers that are configured to negotiate CBC cipher suites shall support this extension as described in [33]

extractions.exact_source_text: The Truncated HMAC extension may be supported if the server communicates with constrained-device clients, cipher suites that use CBC mode are supported, and the server implementation does not support variable-length padding... However, truncated MAC tags shall not be used in conjunction with variable-length padding due to attacks described by Paterson et al. [53].
extractions.explicit_exceptions: if the server communicates with constrained-device clients, cipher suites that use CBC mode are supported, and the server implementation does not support variable-length padding
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: attacks described by Paterson et al. [53]; forging a MAC tag
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: truncated MAC tags shall not be used in conjunction with variable-length padding

extractions.exact_source_text: TLS servers that support TLS 1.3 and the Pre-Shared Key extension shall support this extension.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Applies to TLS version 1.3; TLS servers that support TLS 1.3 and the Pre-Shared Key extension
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: shall support this extension

extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: only RSA key transport cipher suites from the following list may be used... It is recommended that agencies transition to a new method to meet their needs as soon as it is practical

extractions.exact_source_text: For the Federal Government, a security strength of at least 112 bits is required at this time for applying cryptographic protection (e.g., for encrypting or signing data).
extractions.explicit_exceptions: prior to 2014, a security strength of at least 80 bits was required... The processing of this already-protected data at the lower security strength is allowed, but a certain amount of risk must be accepted
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: captured (by an adversary) at that time and later decrypted by that adversary when the algorithm was no longer considered secure
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: a security strength of at least 112 bits is required at this time for applying cryptographic protection

extractions.exact_source_text: The latest revision of SP 800-67 disallows the use of two-key TDEA for applying cryptographic protection and restricts the use of three-key TDEA for applying cryptographic protection to no more than 2^20 data blocks using a single key bundle... Encryption using two-key TDEA is disallowed. Decryption using two-key TDEA is allowed for legacy use using the modes of operation specified in SP 800-38A. Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, encryption using three-key TDEA is deprecated through December 31, 2023 using the approved encryption modes... Three-key TDEA may continue to be used for encryption in existing applications but shall not be used for encryption in new applications. After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for encryption unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance. Decryption using three-key TDEA is allowed for legacy use. The use of SKIPJACK for encryption is disallowed. The use of SKIPJACK for decryption is allowed for legacy use. The use of AES-128, AES-192, AES-256 is acceptable for encryption and decryption using the approved modes in the SP 800-38 series of publications.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Decryption using two-key TDEA and three-key TDEA allowed for legacy use; After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for encryption unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: Sweet32 / block limit; security strength of 80 bits is now considered inadequate
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Three-key TDEA may continue to be used for encryption in existing applications but shall not be used for encryption in new applications. After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for encryption

extractions.exact_source_text: Private-key lengths providing less than 112 bits of security shall not be used to generate digital signatures. Private-key lengths providing at least 112 bits of security are acceptable for the generation of digital signatures. DSA: The DSA domain parameter lengths shall be (2048, 224) or (2048, 256), which provide a security strength of 112 bits; or (3072, 256), which provides a security strength of 128 bits. ECDSA and EdDSA: The security strength provided by an elliptic-curve-based signature algorithm is no greater than 1/2 of the length of the domain parameter n. Therefore, the length of n shall be at least 224 bits to meet the minimum security-strength requirement of 112 bits for Federal Government use... RSA: The length of the modulus n shall be 2048 bits or more to meet the minimum security-strength requirement of 112 bits for Federal Government use. Digital signature verification: Key lengths providing less than 112 bits of security that were previously specified in FIPS 186 are allowed for legacy use when verifying digital signatures... the verification of signatures that used key lengths less than these lower bounds shall be regarded as having unacceptable risks.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Key lengths providing less than 112 bits of security that were previously specified in FIPS 186 are allowed for legacy use when verifying digital signatures (DSA 512-1024, ECDSA 160-223, RSA 1024-2047)
extractions.explicit_attack_or_threat_reference: unacceptable risks for key lengths less than legacy lower bounds
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Private-key lengths providing less than 112 bits of security shall not be used to generate digital signatures. Therefore, the length of n shall be at least 224 bits [ECDSA/EdDSA]... The length of the modulus n shall be 2048 bits or more [RSA]

extractions.exact_source_text: A previous version of SP 800-90A included a fourth algorithm, the DUAL_EC_DRBG, whose use is now disallowed for Federal Government applications... Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, the use of CTR_DRBG using three-key TDEA is deprecated through December 31, 2023. After December 31, 2023, the use of the CTR_DRBG using three-key TDEA is disallowed. The use of CTR_DRBG using AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 is acceptable... The use of the RNGs specified in FIPS 186-2, American National Standard (ANS) X9.31 and the 1998 version of ANS X9.62 are disallowed.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: CTR_DRBG using three-key TDEA is deprecated through December 31, 2023
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: After December 31, 2023, the use of the CTR_DRBG using three-key TDEA is disallowed. The use of CTR_DRBG using AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 is acceptable

extractions.exact_source_text: The use of finite field schemes that support a security strength less than 112 bits is disallowed, i.e., when using the FA domain parameter set specified in previous versions of SP 800-56A: ((len(p), len(q)) = (1024, 160)). The use of the finite field schemes is acceptable when: 1. Using the safe-prime domain-parameter groups listed in Appendix D of SP 800-56A. 2. Using the FB and FC domain parameter sets specified in SP 800-56A, i.e., (len(p), len(q)) = (2048, 224) or (2048, 256). After December 31, 2020, the use of these schemes is disallowed (i.e., all finite field DH and MQV schemes must conform to SP 800-56A). SP 800-56A DH and MQV schemes using elliptic curves: The use of elliptic curve schemes that support a security strength less than 112 bits is disallowed, i.e., when len(n) < 224. The use of the elliptic curve schemes for key agreement that provide at least 112 bits of security strength is acceptable when using the elliptic curves listed in SP 800-56A or when using curves that satisfy the requirements of IG A.2. Non-compliant DH and MQV schemes using elliptic curves... After December 31, 2020, all of these schemes are disallowed.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: After December 31, 2020, all of these schemes are disallowed (must conform to SP 800-56A)
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: all finite field DH and MQV schemes must conform to SP 800-56A

extractions.exact_source_text: SP 800-56B RSA key-agreement and key transport schemes: The use of these schemes is disallowed if len(n) < 2048. The use of these schemes is acceptable if len(n) >= 2048. Non-SP 800 56B-compliant RSA key-agreement and key-transport schemes: The use of these schemes is disallowed if len(n) < 2048. Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, uses of PKCS 1, version 1.5 and other RSA key-agreement or key-transport schemes that are not compliant with SP 800-56B are deprecated. After December 31, 2023, the use of PKCS1-v 1_5 padding scheme is disallowed. After December 31, 2020, the use of other RSA key-agreement or key-transport schemes that are not compliant with SP 800-56B are disallowed.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: PKCS1-v1_5 padding deprecated through December 31, 2023; disallowed after 2023; other non-compliant schemes disallowed after December 31, 2020
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: After December 31, 2023, the use of PKCS1-v 1_5 padding scheme is disallowed

extractions.exact_source_text: The use of two-key TDEA for key wrapping is disallowed. The use of two-key TDEA for unwrapping keying material is allowed for legacy use. Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, key wrapping using three-key TDEA is deprecated through December 31, 2023. After December 31, 2023, the use of three-key TDEA is disallowed for key wrapping unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance. Key unwrapping using three-key TDEA is allowed for legacy use. The use of AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 for both the wrapping and unwrapping of keying material is acceptable.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: Key unwrapping using two-key and three-key TDEA allowed for legacy use; After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA disallowed unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: After December 31, 2023, the use of three-key TDEA is disallowed for key wrapping

extractions.exact_source_text: The length of the key-derivation key shall be at least 112 bits. The use of HMAC-based KDFs is acceptable using a hash function specified in FIPS 180 or FIPS 202 with a key whose length is at least 112 bits. The use of two-key TDEA as the block cipher algorithm in a CMAC-based KDF is disallowed. Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, the use of three-key TDEA is deprecated through December 31, 2023... After December 31, 2023, the use of three-key TDEA is disallowed unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance. The use of AES-128, AES-192, AES-256 is acceptable.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: three-key TDEA deprecated through December 31, 2023
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: The length of the key-derivation key shall be at least 112 bits... After December 31, 2023, the use of three-key TDEA is disallowed

extractions.exact_source_text: SHA-1 for digital signature generation: SHA-1 may only be used for digital signature generation where specifically allowed by NIST protocol-specific guidance. For all other applications, SHA-1 is disallowed for digital signature generation. SHA-1 for digital signature verification: When used for digital signature verification, SHA-1 is allowed for legacy use. SHA-1 for non-digital signature applications: For non-digital-signature applications, the use of SHA-1 is acceptable for applications that do not require collision resistance. SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224, and SHA-512/256: The use of these hash functions is acceptable for all hash function applications. SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, and SHA3-512: The use of these hash functions is acceptable for all hash function applications. TupleHash and ParallelHash: The use of TupleHash and ParallelHash is acceptable for the purposes specified in SP 800-185.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: SHA-1 may only be used for digital signature generation where specifically allowed by NIST protocol-specific guidance; SHA-1 allowed for legacy verification; SHA-1 acceptable for non-digital signature applications that do not require collision resistance
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: For all other applications, SHA-1 is disallowed for digital signature generation

extractions.exact_source_text: HMAC Generation: Keys less than 112 bits in length are disallowed for HMAC generation. The use of key lengths >= 112 bits is acceptable for HMAC generation. HMAC Verification: The use of key lengths < 112 bits for HMAC verification is allowed for legacy use. The use of key lengths >= 112 bits for HMAC verification is acceptable. CMAC Generation: The use of two-key TDEA for CMAC generation is disallowed. Effective as of the final publication of this revision of SP 800-131A, the use of three-key TDEA for CMAC generation is deprecated through December 31, 2023. Three-key TDEA may be used for CMAC generation in existing applications but shall not be used in new applications. After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for CMAC generation unless specifically allowed by other NIST guidance. The use of AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 for CMAC generation is acceptable. CMAC Verification: The use of two-key TDEA and three-key TDEA for CMAC verification is allowed for legacy use. The use of AES for CMAC verification is acceptable. GMAC Generation and Verification: The use of GMAC for MAC generation and verification is acceptable when using AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256. KMAC Generation and Verification: Keys less than 112 bits in length are disallowed for KMAC generation. The use of key lengths >= 112 bits is acceptable for KMAC generation.
extractions.explicit_exceptions: HMAC/CMAC verification with < 112 bits allowed for legacy use; three-key TDEA deprecated through December 31, 2023
extractions.explicit_remediation_stated: Keys less than 112 bits in length are disallowed for HMAC generation... Three-key TDEA may be used for CMAC generation in existing applications but shall not be used in new applications. After December 31, 2023, three-key TDEA is disallowed for CMAC generation
